ticket. Public identifiers only: order numbers and ticket codes, not ids.

CaseCreate.description:
What the requester sends. Context comes from the page the case was
opened on (§4.13), so the client fills it in, never the user.

Attendee cases name at least one of event, order or ticket: that is how
the case finds the organizer who must answer it. A guest proves the order
is theirs with the order's signed link token.
CaseCreate.title: CaseCreate

CaseUpdate.description:

ChecklistRead.description: §4.5 "The organizer shall see an activation checklist": §3.2's five steps.
ChecklistRead.title: ChecklistRead

EventCreate.description:
What an organizer sends to create a draft.

No organizer id and no status: the owner comes from the access token, and
every event starts as a draft. Status changes go through dedicated actions.
`slug` is optional: left out, one is made from the title.

description and category stay optional here although the web form
requires them: a draft saved through the API may be incomplete. The
length limits are the same as the form's.
EventCreate.title: EventCreate

LoginRequest.description:

Inherits the email normalisation from UserBase so a login and the account
it belongs to agree on what the address is.

MeRead.description:
GET /users/me: the account plus what it may do, so a client derives
roles from the real session instead of a local fixture (audit #9).
Event admin is per event, so it is not here: see GET /staff/events.
MeRead.title: MeRead

MyTicketRead.description: A ticket in GET /users/me/tickets, including gifted/group tickets.
MyTicketRead.title: MyTicketRead

OrderEvent.description: Enough of the event to render an order without a second request.

PasswordResetRequest.description: POST /auth/password-reset: the address to send a link to.
PasswordResetRequest.title: PasswordResetRequest

PaymentCase.description:
A support case about the payment's order: its existence and state only.

Attendee cases are read by the attendee and the event's organizer
(06-support.md, "Authorization"); an admin reviewing a payment learns that
a case exists and where it stands, never what was written in it.
PaymentCase.title: PaymentCase

PromoQuote.description:
What the attendee is shown before paying (§4.14): the code, the
discount and the new total. Computed by the server, and computed again at
checkout; nothing here is trusted back.
PromoQuote.title: PromoQuote

PromoQuoteRequest.description:
Exactly one of `code` (typed) or `token` (from a Campaign QR link).
`items` may be empty: the page applies a scanned code before the attendee
has chosen anything.
PromoQuoteRequest.title: PromoQuoteRequest

RefreshRequest.description:
Body for POST /auth/refresh.

Optional because browsers send the refresh token as a cookie instead and
post no body at all; only clients in bearer mode fill this in.
RefreshRequest.title: RefreshRequest

ScanResponse.description:
One of six outcomes (§4.8's five plus wrong_event). `ticket` is present
whenever the code resolved to a real ticket, so the operator sees whose it is
even on a rejection.
ScanResponse.title: ScanResponse

SimulatedPayment.description: The outcome to simulate. Lets the demo show the decline path (§4.10).
SimulatedPayment.title: SimulatedPayment

TimelineEntry.description:
§4.16: "a timestamp, acting user, action type, affected entity, and
short description".
TimelineEntry.title: TimelineEntry

TokenResponse.description:
The answer to a login or a refresh.

Which optional half is populated says how the caller was served. In bearer
mode `refresh_token` is present and the client stores both. In cookie mode
the refresh token goes out as an httpOnly cookie and never appears here,
and `csrf_token` carries the value to echo back on the next refresh.
TokenResponse.title: TokenResponse

UserUpdate.description:
PATCH /users/me. Omitted fields are left alone; email and password
have their own flows.
UserUpdate.title: UserUpdate

post.description:
§4.12 "Suspend users". A suspended account cannot sign in or act: every
authenticated route goes through get_current_active_user.

Exchange credentials for an access/refresh pair.

The password is checked before the status is, so a suspended account is only
distinguishable to someone who already knows its password (01-identity.md:
suspension must not be distinguishable to strangers).
Revoke active refresh token(s) for both cookie and bearer clients and clear cookie.

Email a reset link (§4.1). The same 202 whether or not the address has
an account, so this cannot be used to learn who is registered.

schema.title: Response Request Password Reset Api V1 Auth Password Reset Post

post.description: Set a new password with the emailed token. The link works once.

Trade a refresh token for a fresh pair, rotating and invalidating the old token.

The token comes from the body for clients in bearer mode and from the
httpOnly cookie for browsers. A cookie-borne token additionally has to pass
the CSRF check, because unlike a body it is sent without the caller asking.

The status is re-read here rather than trusted from the token, so suspending
an account takes effect at the next refresh instead of at the token's expiry.

Create an account. The new user is active but not email-verified; a
verification link is emailed (§4.1).
Mark the address verified with the emailed token (§4.1).
